title: Scalars and Vectors
learning_goal: Distinguish scalar and vector quantities and combine perpendicular vectors graphically and with the Pythagorean theorem.

stages.title: 1. Scalar or vector?
stages.content: A scalar has magnitude only. Examples include mass, time, temperature, distance, and speed. A vector has magnitude and direction. Examples include displacement, velocity, acceleration, and force.

stages.title: 2. Why direction matters
stages.content: Two vectors can have the same magnitude but represent different physical situations if their directions differ. A velocity of 20 m/s east is not the same vector as 20 m/s west.

stages.title: 3. Worked example
stages.content: A student walks 3 m east and then 4 m north. The total distance traveled is 7 m, but the displacement is the straight-line vector from start to finish. Because the two legs are perpendicular, the displacement magnitude is √(3² + 4²) = 5 m, directed northeast.

stages.title: 4. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A drone moves 6 m east and 8 m north. What is the magnitude of its displacement?
stages.hint: The east and north displacements form the two perpendicular legs of a right triangle.
stages.alternate_explanation: Draw a right triangle. The resultant displacement is the hypotenuse, so combine the perpendicular components using the Pythagorean theorem.

stages.title: 5. Combine vectors graphically
stages.content: To add vectors graphically, place the tail of the second vector at the head of the first. The resultant vector points from the starting tail to the final head.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, classify quantities as scalar or vector, explain why direction matters, add perpendicular vectors graphically, and calculate the magnitude of a resultant vector.
